note.question: When will consumers arrive when they fear a shortage?
note.overview: Consider consumers who prefer to consume a good later rather than earlier. If the price is constant, then we would expect consumers to wait to buy the good. That does not hold if consumers are concerned that others will buy the good early, so that a shortage will later occur.

source.quote: Might the firm lose profits by offering advance sales?
Problem definition: Consider consumers who prefer to consume a good later rather than earlier.
The application is important: managers want to know when consumers will arrive, when they should make the product available, and what price to charge to maximize profits.
Analytical results show the effects of the amount of supply on the profit-maximizing price and customers’ behavior.
We let the number of potential buyers be stochastic, allow consumers to choose whether and when to arrive, and let a risk of shortage exist in the first period.
In that case, we refer to a sale in period 1 as an advanced sale.
In equilibrium, in Region 3 (where consumers may arrive in both periods), the aggregate arrival rate λ1 + λ2 increases with the price p.
Second, we assume homoge­ neous consumers and that the price is fixed over all peri­ ods and all consumers, so that price discrimination is impossible.
Hence, from now on, given (v,k), we assume that the demand is high, where by high we mean that λ is large enough so that there is a unique equilibrium and it is of type 1–4.
The equilibrium and, therefore, the utility depend on the region where we end up after sub­ tracting the price p from the initial value v.
